claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 on 2026-09-26, MCP Inspector 2.8.0 was qualified against the installed 2.7.0 and then switched into production. The npm tarball https://registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/inspector/-/inspector-2.8.0.tgz (1,206,059 bytes, sha256 4db39519d276b99fe650f1032a3256cb704648cc611e598a38e178b1ba8a7cbf) had integrity sha512-zn0A8fIrPDge36vId0XMpj0FL0FChIGQvAvV/+iRTvUYkSzTSIALHjhZyLIgKTzBPnzrxDJnfRbrPcElUcXR6Q==, equal to npm dist.integrity; `npm audit signatures` on a scratch install reported 190 packages with verified registry signatures and 34 with verified attestations, including the package's SLSA provenance from .github/workflows/main.yml at refs/tags/2.8.0, commit 1e31c78fbf81a989e8eb47021c6281d7876ad7fd. It was installed from that verified file into a new tools/mcp-inspector-2.8.0 prefix; npm 11 skipped the package's postinstall, which exits at once for a package under node_modules. In a bwrap sandbox with a private loopback-only network, a read-only root, /mnt hidden and MCP_AUTO_OPEN_ENABLED=false, the same 15 gated steps passed on 2.8.0 and on 2.7.0 with identical exit codes and, once per-run paths and markers were normalized, identical outputs: over stdio against a scratch QMD 2.8.3 index, tools/list (get, multi_get, query, status), tools/call query (one hit), an unknown tool (exit 5, tool_not_found), resources/list, prompts/list and tools/list --strict; over streamable HTTP to `qmd mcp --http`, tools/list and tools/call with the default and the auto protocol era. With a scratch API token and DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH set to false, 0 or yes, the 2.7.0 web server printed 'Auth: disabled (DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH)' and answered GET /api/config with 200 without a token and with a wrong one, while 2.8.0 answered 401 in both cases and 200 with the right token; both disabled the gate for true and kept it when the variable was unset, and no start printed 'Opening browser'. With no Inspector process running and nothing but bin/mcp-inspector naming the 2.7.0 prefix, bin/mcp-inspector was relinked to tools/mcp-inspector-2.8.0 at 2026-09-26T04:51:23Z; through the PATH entry, `npm ls` read 2.8.0 and the stdio tools/list, tools/call and unknown-tool checks passed.

Local integration evidence with synthetic fixtures: the upstream suite (npm run local:gate) was not run on this host. The HTTP arm used a scratch QMD server without OAuth; SSE, OAuth, remote servers, the web UI pages, the MCP Apps sandbox and the TUI were not exercised. The measured auth difference does not change this host's live exposure: no client configuration here sets DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH, and agents run the Inspector in --cli mode. It matters when someone sets the variable to a false-looking value to keep the token gate on.
